LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 4.3.1 WORD CLASSES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words do we use to refer to people or things without saying who or what they are exactly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text
2. use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 4.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 4.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes to a partner. (skill: use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text.
3. Practise this skill: use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words do we use to refer to people or things without saying who or what they are exactly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Classes means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify relative and indefinite pronouns in a text.
5. Be able to: use relative and indefinite pronouns correctly in oral and written texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
